text:
maya: heads up — eval CI fired an alert: quantized-ggml canary shows ~8% drop in answer_f1 vs baseline after last deploy. seeing this on the long-tail QA prompts.

devon: ok which deploy/commit? any recent changes to runner or CI plumber?

maya: deploy was 2026-02-03 12:34 UTC, tag: deploy/quant-canary-20260203, commits included PR #812 and PR #809. PR #812 changed the CI orchestrator polling/heartbeat.

liam: fwiw PR #812 moved the orchestrator poll interval from 10s -> 2s and lowered RPC retry backoff to speed job turnover. could be noisy for KV cache warmups.

eval-bot: Automated CI alert — job eval/runner-quant-ci #452 failed
- failure mode: metric_regression(answer_f1) > threshold (8.1%)
- most recent run: https://ci.redwood/test/452
- logs excerpt:
```
[2026-02-03T12:34:12Z] runner: starting eval batch id=337
[2026-02-03T12:34:13Z] kvcache: miss spike=0.42
[2026-02-03T12:34:13Z] rpc: connection reset by peer
[2026-02-03T12:34:13Z] runner: aborting batch id=337 reason=orchestrator_poll_timeout
```

sophia: I repro locally with quantized-ggml and the new orchestrator config — when poll interval is 2s we see repeated cache evictions and token generation latency spikes, results diverge.

devon: can we bisect quickly between the previous stable and the canary? try git bisect between b8d2f77 (stable) and c3f9a2b (canary head). devon: starting bisect now.

devon: quick bisect result: regression starts at commit c3f9a2b -> PR #812 (orchestrator poll/backoff changes).

liam: that aligns w/ hypothesis. PR #809 was the quant kernel fallback tuning (separate) — that one passed local evals. #812 is the main suspect.

maya: what are mitigation options?

sophia: short term: revert PR #812 or flip feature flag orchestrator.fast_poll=false for the canary pool, and increase rpc timeout to 10s to avoid mid-step disconnects. Longer: make KV cache sticky across rapid reconnects.

devon: I'm opening a rollback PR now: revert PR #812 (branch: rollback/orchestrator-poll-fix). also creating a hold on the quant canary rollout.

oncall-bot: @oncall paging — rollback PR opened: https://git.redwood/pulls/2987 — action: rollback orchestrator poll changes on canary pool.

maya: deploying rollback to canary in 2m. will monitor answer_f1 and smoke.

liam: after rollback we should add an eval CI test that runs a short steady-state run with rapid connect/disconnect to catch this. also add metric for kvcache_miss_rate in console dashboards (per-runner).

maya: agreed. creating follow-up ticket to add the steady-state flakiness test and dashboard gating. ticket: ENG-ML-1429.

eval-bot: canary rollback deployed to pool quant-canary-2 at 12:48 UTC. re-run scheduled.

maya: re-run results (12:56 UTC): answer_f1 back within 0.6% of baseline, kvcache_miss_rate normalized. marking incident as resolved and holding the wider rollout.

sophia: notes: root cause = aggressive orchestrator poll/backoff change causing transient RPC drop/connects -> KV cache misses -> degraded outputs in quantized path.

devon: action items: (1) keep PR #812 reverted until we have sticky cache or reconnection preservation (2) add flakiness CI test (3) dashboard metric and alert for kvcache_miss_rate.

maya: thanks all — will update the postmortem doc and set the release hold. :thumbsup:
